rounds.name: Worker-Lowell
rounds.text:
Since we have no history with Worker‑Lowell, we should encourage thorough work by withholding pay, which yields the highest payoff when they do the job properly and still gives a small benefit if they cut corners.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Greer
rounds.text:
Since we have no history with Worker‑Greer, we should assume they are as likely to cut corners as to do the job properly; the expected payoff is higher when we WITHHOLD (5 vs 1) than when we TRUST (3 vs 0).  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Arden
rounds.text:
Since this is the first interaction with Worker‑Arden, I have no evidence of their reliability, and withholding pay gives a higher reward both when they work properly (5 vs 3) and when they cut corners (1 vs 0). Thus the safe dominant choice is to withhold.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Ives
rounds.text:
Since we have no history with Worker‑Ives, we can’t gauge their reliability; however, withholding pay gives a higher minimum payoff (1 vs 0) and a higher maximum payoff (5 vs 3) regardless of their behavior. Therefore the safe, higher‑expected choice is to withhold.

rounds.name: Worker-Jarvis
rounds.text:
Since I have no history with Worker‑Jarvis, I can’t gauge their honesty, but withholding pay always yields at least as many completed tasks as trusting (5 vs 3 if they work properly, 1 vs 0 if they cut corners). Therefore the safest choice is to withhold.

rounds.name: Worker-Flint
rounds.text:

ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Calder
rounds.text:
we should choose the action that gives the higher payoff in both possible worker outcomes. Withholding pay yields 5 completed tasks if they work properly and still gives 1 task if they cut corners, which dominates trusting (3 or 0). Therefore the safe optimal choice is to withhold.

rounds.name: Worker-Kerr
rounds.text:
Since we have no history with Worker‑Kerr, withholding pay gives the strongest incentive for them to do the job properly (5 tasks versus only 3 if we trust). Even if they cut corners, we still get 1 task instead of 0.
